task: Decouple provider-level config from project/tooling config in the profile system (ConfigLoader/ProviderProfile) and add a migration so users can switch providers while preserving shared project/assistant/skills config.

key_reasoning.reason: Touches the config schema (src/env/types.ts), ConfigLoader (src/utils/config.ts), the migration framework (src/migrations/*), the CLI layer (profile/*, assistants/setup/*, skills/setup/*), and potentially all 7 provider plugins that consume ProviderProfile via exportEnvVars/agentHooks — a core shared contract used across nearly every subsystem.

Per technical-analysis.md risk indicators, the exact target schema shape and which currently profile-scoped fields (codeMieProject, codeMieIntegration, hooks, plugins, assistants.maxHistoryMessages, skillsSearchUrl, claudeAutocompactPct, metrics) count as 'project-level' vs. legitimately provider-scoped is not yet decided — an architectural design decision, not just an implementation detail.

The direction of split requested (decoupling provider identity/credentials from project/tooling context within ProviderProfile, likely via a new linked/shared structure) is a different shape of change than the existing migration-004 precedent (flat move-to-top-level). ConfigLoader.load()'s merge/priority logic is intricate, branchy, and only partially covered by tests, raising regression risk on a widely-used code path.

Technical-analysis.md's own summary estimates 6+ files as a floor (schema, ConfigLoader, new migration file, its test, one or more CLI touch points) before confirming whether any of the 7 provider plugins' exportEnvVars/agentHooks call sites also need updates — realistic estimate spans multiple subsystems, likely 11-15 files.

Configuration/data layer, migration-framework layer, CLI layer (profile + assistants/setup + skills/setup), and provider-plugin layer are all implicated — a significant config-schema restructuring analogous to a database schema change, with cross-cutting impact across layers.

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from XL to XXL: task is explicitly framed as a migration/decoupling ('migration', 'decouple') of a core shared subsystem (ProviderProfile/ConfigLoader) consumed by the CLI, migration framework, and every provider plugin.
Technical Risk bumped from M to L: the ProviderProfile/MultiProviderConfig schema is being significantly restructured, equivalent to a database schema change.
Technical Risk bumped from L to XL: task explicitly requires a data migration to preserve existing users' shared project/assistant/skills config while decoupling provider identity.

File Change Estimate bumped from L to XL: data migration requirement adds a new numbered migration file, its dedicated test, and updates across every consuming call site (schema, loader, CLI, provider plugins).

Affected Layers bumped from L to XL: the config-schema change is treated as a significant schema/persistence change (per guide: 'DB schema changes always bump Affected Layers to at least L'), and it spans config, migration, CLI, and provider-plugin layers simultaneously.

Requirements Clarity bumped from L to XL: vague acceptance criteria — exact target schema shape and field classification (project-level vs. provider-scoped) are undecided per technical-analysis.md risk indicators.
split_recommendation: Recommend splitting by phase, mirroring the tested migration-004/005 pattern: (1) Spec/design the new decoupled schema — decide exactly which fields move to a shared project/workspace structure vs. remain provider-scoped, and how multiple provider profiles link to one shared context; (2) Implement the new schema types + ConfigLoader read/merge logic for the decoupled shape, additive/parallel to the existing flat schema; (3) Implement the numbered migration (e.g. 006-...) with dedicated unit tests, following the tested pattern of migrations 004/005 rather than the untested pattern of 001-003; (4) Update the CLI layer (profile switch/display, assistants/setup, skills/setup) to read/write the new shape; (5) Update provider-plugin call sites (exportEnvVars/agentHooks) across all 7 provider plugins to consume the decoupled config, verifying the blast radius flagged as unconfirmed in technical-analysis.md.
